items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: reading comic books and reading magazines and reading just kids books and whatever, the war that you read about was the first World War and the brave marines at The Somme or whatever it was, and the Red Baron flying the airplanes and so forth.

ctx.x: By a year, okay. Can you recall back then thinking that that was going to be a possibility if this war doesn’t wind down or end? Was that a concern of yours?

Well it wasn’t a concern. When I was 14 years old I was afraid the war would be over before I could get into it. You know, I was a kid. I wanted to be a glory boy, I wanted to fly airplanes, I wanted whatever it was. Because you remember, I was brought up on World War I pop literature. You were always reading — you remember World War I, during the thirties, when I was a kid, reading comic books and reading magazines and reading just kids books and whatever, the war that you read about was the first World War and…
Well as long as we’re in this sort of part of your life, do you remember what it cost to go to Hamilton at the time?
